**1. Survey overview**

The survey was distributed to all permanent and casual staff at the Brisbane Distribution Centre (BDC) on Monday 10 March 2025, with reminders sent on Wednesday 12 March. The survey closed at 17:00 on Friday 14 March 2025.

- Temperature control and monitoring
- Equipment reliability
- Cold chain procedures and training
- Communication and shift handover
- Overall satisfaction

Where a comment could not be read clearly, it is marked [illegible].*

**On equipment alarms and response times (Item: "Equipment alarms are acted on promptly")**

- "Alarms go off and then someone has to walk over to the freezer to see what it is. There is no screen at the desk that shows the alarm code. So it takes longer than it should to fix the problem." – Picking, night shift
- "The alarm went off on the 4th and the backup chiller didn't start on its own. That is the main reason I said disagree. If the power had gone out it would have been bad." – Loading dock, day shift
- "I have been here 9 years and the alarms have always been responded to. I think the issue is that people don't know the new alarm codes since the system update." – Freezer, day shift

**On freezer door seals (Item: "Freezer door seals are in good condition")**

- "The seals are cracked and you can see ice build up on the frame. It makes the freezer work harder to hold temp. I have mentioned it twice to my supervisor." – Freezer, day shift
- "One of the seals on door 3 is hanging off. Someone put tape on it but the tape came off within a week." – Picking, afternoon shift

documents.title: Cold Chain Operations Survey 2025 - Responses
documents.content:
COLD CHAIN OPERATIONS SURVEY 2025 – RESPONSES  
Brisbane Distribution Centre  
Survey window: 10–14 March 2025  
Report compiled: 17 March 2025  
Owner: Operations Review Team

---

**1. Survey overview**

The survey was distributed to all permanent and casual staff at the Brisbane Distribution Centre (BDC) on Monday 10 March 2025, with reminders sent on Wednesday 12 March. The survey closed at 17:00 on Friday 14 March 2025.

A total of 47 participants completed the survey. Brisbane Distribution Centre participant_count_in_survey 47 participants. Record status: current. This response count is current and final for the March 2025 survey round; no further responses were accepted after the close time.

The survey was conducted anonymously via paper forms and an online link. Staff were advised that individual responses would not be identifiable in any report. The survey covered the following areas:

- Temperature control and monitoring
- Equipment reliability
- Cold chain procedures and training
- Communication and shift handover
- Overall satisfaction

---

**2. Participation by shift and role**

The table below shows the breakdown of the 47 responses by shift pattern and role category. Some respondents did not provide a role, and one did not specify a shift.

| Shift pattern | Permanent | Casual | Not stated | Total |
|---------------|-----------|--------|------------|-------|
| Day (06:00–14:00) | 12 | 4 | 0 | 16 |
| Afternoon (14:00–22:00) | 9 | 3 | 1 | 13 |
| Night (22:00–06:00) | 8 | 2 | 0 | 10 |
| Rotating / variable | 3 | 2 | 0 | 5 |
| Not stated | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 |
| **Total** | **33** | **12** | **2** | **47** |

Role categories were grouped into: picking/packing, loading dock, quality control, maintenance, and supervisory. The largest group was picking/packing (n=19), followed by loading dock (n=11), quality control (n=6), maintenance (n=5), supervisory (n=4), and other/not stated (n=2).

---

**3. Response rates by area**

| Area | Invited | Completed | Response rate |
|------|---------|-----------|---------------|
| Picking/packing | 26 | 19 | 73% |
| Loading dock | 14 | 11 | 79% |
| Quality control | 7 | 6 | 86% |
| Maintenance | 6 | 5 | 83% |
| Supervisory | 4 | 4 | 100% |
| Other | 3 | 2 | 67% |
| **Total** | **60** | **47** | **78%** |

Note: the invitation count of 60 includes staff who were on leave or secondment during the survey window. Three staff members were on leave for the full week and were not sent reminders.

---

**4. Likert scale results (summary)**

Respondents were asked to rate statements on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree). The table below shows the mean score and the distribution for each statement. n = 47 for all items unless noted.

| Statement | Mean | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | n/a |
|-----------|------|---|---|---|---|---|-----|
| Temperature logs are completed accurately on my shift | 3.8 | 1 | 3 | 9 | 21 | 12 | 1 |
| Temperature alarms are responded to promptly | 3.5 | 2 | 5 | 14 | 16 | 9 | 1 |
| I have received adequate training on cold chain procedures | 3.9 | 1 | 2 | 8 | 22 | 13 | 1 |
| Equipment (reefers, chillers, temp probes) is reliable | 3.2 | 4 | 8 | 15 | 12 | 6 | 2 |
| Shift handover includes relevant temperature information | 3.6 | 1 | 4 | 12 | 18 | 10 | 2 |
| I know who to contact if I notice a temperature issue | 4.1 | 0 | 2 | 5 | 24 | 15 | 1 |
| Cold chain procedures are followed consistently on all shifts | 3.3 | 3 | 7 | 12 | 16 | 7 | 2 |

documents.content:
- "Temp is fine on our line, we check the probes every 2hrs and they are always in range. The only drama is when we are short staffed and the check gets done late." – Picking, day shift
- "Chiller 3 runs a bit warm in the arvo when the dock doors are open. We flag it on the board but it always comes right by the time the next check is due. Not a drama, just something we watch." – Loading dock, afternoon shift
- "I have worked at three DC's and this one is the best for keeping things cold. The old place used to drop to 6 degrees all the time. Here we are steady at 2-4." – Quality control, day shift
- "The temp control is adequate. We have the odd alarm but they are usually a door being left open or a probe that needs a clean. Nothing that has ever caused us to reject stock." – Supervisory, night shift
- "Would be good if the chillers got serviced more often in summer. They cop a hiding when it hits 35 outside. But the temps still hold, so it is more about noise than product safety." – Maintenance, day shift
- "When the alarm goes off at 3am you better be quick or the supervisor gets a call. But that is fair enough. The product is the priority." – Loading dock, night shift
- "I have seen the temp records from last year and they are all within spec. The auditors were happy. That tells you the system is working." – Quality control, day shift

**Training and procedures (n=7)**

- "The training video is a bit old but the message is still the same. I would rather have the hands-on session with Dave from QC, he knows his stuff." – Picking, day shift
- "New starters should get a refresher after 3 months. I remember the basics but not all the detail about what to do if a reefer fails." – Loading dock, afternoon shift

**Cold Chain Operations Survey 2025 – Responses**

**Survey period:** 10–14 March 2025
**Location:** Brisbane Distribution Centre (BDC)
**Method:** Anonymous paper survey distributed to all shifts; 47 responses received of 52 staff on roster (90% response rate).
**Note:** Results below update and partially supersede the February 2025 pulse check. Where a change in position is noted, it reflects the combined survey and follow-up feedback, not a single comment.

---

**Summary of responses – Question 1: "Overall, is temperature control at BDC adequate for cold chain compliance?"**

| Response | Feb 2025 pulse (n=31) | Mar 2025 survey (n=47) | Change |

| Unsure / mixed | 4 (13%) | 11 (23%) | +10 pts |

**Position statement (current):** The overall position on the temperature issue at Brisbane Distribution Centre has shifted from adequate to adequate but with concerns. This is based on the March survey results and the follow-up comments below, which show a clear minority view that freezer door seals and chiller response times need attention. **Question 3 (continued) – Free-text comments on temperature control**

Some comments touch on more than one item; these have been allocated to the primary topic only. Spelling and grammar are as provided by respondents. Where a comment could not be read clearly, it is marked [illegible].*

**On equipment alarms and response times (Item: "Equipment alarms are acted on promptly")**

- "Alarms go off and then someone has to walk over to the freezer to see what it is. There is no screen at the desk that shows the alarm code. So it takes longer than it should to fix the problem." – Picking, night shift
- "The alarm went off on the 4th and the backup chiller didn't start on its own. That is the main reason I said disagree. If the power had gone out it would have been bad." – Loading dock, day shift
- "I have been here 9 years and the alarms have always been responded to. I think the issue is that people don't know the new alarm codes since the system update." – Freezer, day shift

**On freezer door seals (Item: "Freezer door seals are in good condition")**

- "The seals are cracked and you can see ice build up on the frame. It makes the freezer work harder to hold temp. I have mentioned it twice to my supervisor." – Freezer, day shift
- "One of the seals on door 3 is hanging off. Someone put tape on it but the tape came off within a week." – Picking, afternoon shift
- "I don't work in the freezer so I can't say. I left it blank." – Admin

**On temperature logs and daily reviews (Item: "Temperature logs are reviewed daily")**

- "The logs are done but I don't know if anyone actually looks at them. We fill them in and put them in the folder." – Loading dock, morning shift
- "The supervisor checks them at the start of each shift. That is good." – Freezer, night shift
- "We are supposed to check them but sometimes we are short staffed and it doesn't happen until later in the day." – Maintenance, day shift

- "Everyone knows to call the supervisor. That is not the problem. The problem is the supervisor has to call maintenance and maintenance takes time to come." – Picking, day shift
- "There is a list on the wall but it is out of date. It still has the old maintenance manager's name on it." – Freezer, day shift
- "I know who to call but I don't always have a radio. If I have to leave the freezer to find someone, the temp could keep dropping." – Freezer, afternoon shift

- "It did not start on the 4th. I saw the alarm and went to check. The unit was in manual mode. Someone had left it in manual after the last test." – Maintenance, day shift
- "I don't know what the backup chiller is. I only work in the warehouse." – Picking, morning shift

- "Someone shut the freezer door and it didn't seal properly. I mentioned it in the pass-down but I don't think it went anywhere. Same door as before." – Freezer, night shift
- "I saw a pallet of ice cream sitting in the shade outside the dock door. It was there for maybe 20 minutes. I didn't report it because I was told off last time for making a fuss." – Loading dock, morning shift
- "The temp in the chiller was 6.5 for about an hour on the 12th. I told the supervisor and he said he'd log it. I checked the log later and it wasn't there." – Freezer, afternoon shift

**Comments on overall satisfaction:**

- "It's better than it was a year ago but we still have a long way to go. The new chiller helps but the old one should be replaced, not patched up." – Maintenance, day shift
- "I'm satisfied most days but the summer months are hard. The dock gets hot and the doors are open too long." – Loading dock, afternoon shift
- "The freezers are fine. I don't understand what all the fuss is about. I've worked here 20 years and we never had these issues before." – Freezer, night shift
- "Neutral. The system works when everyone does their job but there are too many shortcuts being taken." – Picking, day shift
- "I'm not satisfied. The backup chiller failed on the 4th and that should never happen. Someone should have checked it after the last test." – Maintenance, day shift
- "Very satisfied. The team is doing a great job under difficult circumstances." – Admin

---

**Question 7 – "Do you have any suggestions for improving temperature control or cold chain operations?" (Open text)**

**Themes identified across all responses (n = 59 total surveys returned):**

| Theme | Number of comments |
|---|---|
| More frequent testing/maintenance of backup equipment | 12 |
| Better staffing during peak hours | 9 |
| Replace or repair dock seals and doors | 8 |
| Improve communication between shifts | 7 |
| More training for new staff | 6 |
| Update the contact list on the wall | 5 |
| Faster response from maintenance | 4 |
| Other / general | 8 |

**Selected verbatim comments:**

- "Test the backup chiller more than once a month. It failed on the 4th because it was left in manual. That is not good enough."
- "We need more people on the dock in the afternoons. The truck arrives and there is only one person to unload and the door stays open too long."
- "Fix door 3. The seal has been hanging off for weeks and tape doesn't work."
- "The pass-down book is good but no one reads it. We write things down and then nothing happens."
- "Give everyone a radio. I can't call for help if I'm in the freezer and something goes wrong."
- "The training was fine but it was two years ago. I would like a refresher."
- "Update the emergency contact list. It still has the old maintenance manager's name on it."
- "The supervisor means well but he has too much to do. Give him some help."
- "Cold chain is everyone's job, not just the freezer staff. The dock people need to understand why the door can't stay open."
- "I think we are doing okay. Just keep the equipment serviced and we'll be right."
